A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GOAT research, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Existing material can be matched across pagination and appendix renumbering, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on C4 language modeling, synthetic retrieval, genome modeling, ImageNet, and a synthetic copy-mixture task.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds FineWeb results, quantitative ablations, training analyses, and spatial VQA results.

M1.justification: Section 4 adds an optional explicit first-token bias to the specified sink parameterization and describes mixed 2D image and 1D text positions for multimodal attention. The central Fourier-prior SDPA construction remains unchanged. ImageNet's 2D factorization already appeared in v1; its expanded explanation does not establish a changed implementation.

E1.justification: v2 adds language modeling on the FineWeb corpus and a distinct multimodal task: spatial questions about CIFAR-10 image arrangements, evaluated under unseen image-token scan orders. These extend the data and task coverage beyond the retained language, retrieval, genome, and ImageNet experiments.

E2.justification: The new spatial VQA comparison evaluates No PE alongside RoPE and GOAT (Table 9), adding a comparator absent from v1's reported experiments. Existing comparator memberships are retained. FineWeb reuses RoPE, while FLT is discussed only as related work, not evaluated.

E3.justification: New protocols include 1.23B-parameter FineWeb models trained at length 2048 and evaluated through 16k, plus spatial VQA with 50k training scenes, 10k test scenes, and validation-NLL checkpoint selection. Appendix I introduces controlled variations in mode count, frequency configuration, and initialization. The existing C4 and ImageNet setup tables retain their settings.

E4.justification: Appendix I adds quantitative tests of Fourier mode count, frequency base, learned frequencies, and initialization, plus learned-head structure and training-loss checkpoint analyses (Tables 3–7). These substantially extend v1's prior visualizations. Appendix K additionally tests spatial VQA under held-out scan orders.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Figure 4 retains averaging over three genome continuations. The new Table 6 standard deviation describes variation across attention heads, not uncertainty across repeated experimental runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds FineWeb results: GOAT/RoPE scores are 20.75/20.82 at 2k and 24.77/417.43 at 16k. Table 9 adds spatial VQA accuracy of 20.3% for GOAT, 17.2% for No PE, and 16.5% for RoPE. Tables 3–7 add ablation and analysis results. Existing Figures 1–5 retain their results; these additions are not revisions of earlier scores.

T1.justification: Theorem 4 changes its stated key-only realization from two padded dimensions in v1 Appendix F.4 to one scalar dimension in v2 Appendix G.4, matching its existing proof. Section 4 adds explicit parameterization equations, although Equation 20 prints cosine–sine products inconsistent with the stated axis-wise extension of Equation 12. The principal EOT, stability, and classification proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about learned attention priors, extrapolation, disentangled sinks, and compatibility with optimized attention kernels. The new experiments support those claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly explains ALiBi's NIAH failures through fixed slopes suppressing distant needles, contrasting this with GOAT's adjustable prior margin. Table 4 attributes frequency-grid robustness to compensation by learned coefficients. Existing interpretations and qualifications otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4 newly specifies the geometric frequency schedule and base, sink-MLP activation and initialization, and normalized position inputs. Tables 8 and 10 provide substantial FineWeb and VQA reproduction details, including architectures, optimization, tokenization or visual codebooks, budgets, and checkpoint selection. The earlier C4/ImageNet configurations and repository link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Appendix A consolidates positioning against additive biases, rotary encodings, attention sinks, and transport interpretations. It adds Choromanski et al. (2024)'s FLT and distinguishes its linear-attention Fourier construction from GOAT's softmax SDPA realization. Most other comparisons and citations were already present.

P1.justification: v2 expands selected method explanations, clarifies one-sided transport, corrects 'scaled' to 'unscaled' scores near Equation 1, and adds related-work and experimental appendix sections. It also updates the publication footer. Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds a substantial set of table displays covering billion-parameter evaluation, ablations, spectral structure, convergence, and VQA results and settings. The five original figures retain their content and design, with resizing or relocation, including Figures 4 and 5. Existing training tables are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v1 offered little quantitative evidence about sensitivity to GOAT's design choices and no billion-parameter evaluation. v2 addresses these gaps with targeted ablations, optimization checkpoints, and the matched FineWeb comparison, substantially strengthening the empirical basis for its design and scalability claims. Spatial VQA and detailed setup tables further improve coverage and assessability. The new Equation 20 inconsistency and continued absence of run-level uncertainty limit confidence, but do not outweigh the substantial evidential gains.
